purpose: Model-level period-register ruler ported from Chronologic-EN (arXiv:2609.23178, code MIT). Two frozen instruments score every passage: a decade-distribution date model (signed residual of its mean year from the target year) and an authentic-vs-LLM-imitation classifier (P(synthetic)). Each candidate becomes a percentile against REAL reference passages in the same log-word-count length bin and within +/-10 years of its target year (ties go against the candidate). A set of candidates is summarised by the W1 distance of its date percentiles from uniform and by its mean authenticity percentile, each read against a noise floor of pseudo-models drawn leave-one-group-out from the reference itself (default 2,000); the pseudo-model means set the 100 point of 0-100 period_fidelity and authenticity_fidelity scores and their 95% interval is reported beside them. Real instruments are the released chronologic/chronologic-date-deberta (T=1.0551) and chronologic-authenticity-deberta checkpoints behind a lazy torch/transformers import; rows that already carry scores (or a --score-cache) run model-free. A third channel, the architecture band (p22 Score A), cuts each candidate into ~1,000-word windows and reads Spec 99-style syntax features (clause depth, hypotaxis, root deferral, dependency distance, sentence-length shape, interruptions) as percentiles against length-matched real windows: in-band share (10th to 90th), signed displacement so overshoot reads as over rather than better, per-feature readings, and a stdlib veto for looping or degraded windows; spaCy en_core_web_sm parses, or rows carry architecture_features. Descriptive validator only: not a reward, not a passage-level detector, does not date a document.
use_when: You have a set of generated passages, each written for a target year, and want to know how far the set sits from real prose of those years
You need a register ruler with length matching, a date window and a measured noise floor (the failures of the earlier wikitext-referenced ruler)
You can supply real dated reference passages with a source group (author or volume) per passage
You want to validate a register-shift training run against held-out authors
do_not_use_when: You want to date or classify a single document (the instruments are model-level)
You want a training reward or a selection objective (validator only; the authenticity half is easy to inflate)
The reference has fewer than two source groups, or no passages near the candidates' target years
You want scores comparable to published Chronologic numbers (those need the Chronologic reference corpus)

inputs.reference: JSONL {id, text, year, group[, date_estimate_year, p_synthetic]}
inputs.score_cache: optional JSONL cache of instrument scores (appended per batch; resumes)

artifacts: results.period_ruler.channels.date: period_fidelity, w1_from_uniform, null interval, drift years
results.period_ruler.channels.architecture: in_band_share, signed_displacement, veto_rate, per_feature, null intervals

compute.cost_note: Two DeBERTa-v3-large forward passes per passage (GPU recommended); model-free when every row carries precomputed scores. The pseudo-model null is pure Python.

examples.description: Score a set of generations against a dated reference pool (loads both instruments)
Date channel only, with per-candidate percentiles for diagnosis

references: Chronologic: Measuring Language Models' Ability to Represent the Past (arXiv:2609.23178): https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23178
